USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Surmountable antagonism

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

An agonist’s concentration–response curve shifts to the right after a second drug is added. The same maximal response can still be achieved by increasing agonist concentration. The antagonist binds reversibly at the agonist site. Which mechanism is demonstrated?

  1. Positive allosteric enhancement
  2. Agonism at every occupied receptor
  3. Reversible competitive antagonism
  4. Irreversible receptor destruction
  5. Noncompetitive reduction of maximal response
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Reversible competitive antagonism

Competition lowers apparent agonist potency but can be overcome with sufficient agonist.

Understanding the options

Reversible competitive antagonism
Competition lowers apparent agonist potency but can be overcome with sufficient agonist.
Irreversible receptor destruction
This is inconsistent with the stated reversible binding.
Noncompetitive reduction of maximal response
The observed maximum remains unchanged.
Positive allosteric enhancement
The curve shifts toward lower apparent potency, not enhancement.
Agonism at every occupied receptor
The second drug blocks rather than activates the receptor.
